quests.contextSentence: Even the most experienced candidates looked anxious in the waiting room before the interviews.
quests.explanation: 'Relaxed' is the everyday word, while 'at ease' is slightly more formal.

quests.contextSentence: Looking back on the argument, he felt proud of how he'd behaved.
quests.explanation: Embarrassment passes quickly, but shame runs deeper and feels more moral.

quests.contextSentence: After months of revision and sleepless nights, she was thrilled with her exam results.
quests.explanation: 'Let down' suggests that someone else failed your expectations.

quests.contextSentence: Our new neighbour is so outgoing that she chats with everyone on the train.
quests.explanation: Introverts recharge alone, and that isn't the same as being shy.

quests.contextSentence: Mornings are hard for him; he's rarely cheerful before ten, and he never chats at breakfast.
quests.explanation: Among friends 'grumpy' is casual; in writing prefer 'irritable' or 'bad-tempered'.

quests.contextSentence: Despite two failed launches and a shrinking budget, she remained hopeful about the future.
quests.explanation: The suffixes do the work: -ful means full of and -less means without, as in careful/careless.

quests.contextSentence: When we arrived in the village, the locals were friendly and invited us to dinner.
quests.explanation: 'Unfriendly' is mild, whereas 'hostile' suggests open aggression or strong opposition.

quests.contextSentence: As teenagers in the same small town, the two sisters were inseparable.
quests.explanation: 'Estranged' means no longer speaking, usually after a fight.

quests.contextSentence: When a deadline is at risk, you can count on her; she's really dependable.
quests.explanation: 'Flaky' is informal, while 'unreliable' is the neutral choice.

quests.contextSentence: To keep a team motivated, a good manager should be open-minded about new ideas.
quests.explanation: 'Set in your ways' is an idiom for someone unlikely to change habits.

quests.contextSentence: Even after winning the national award for the third year running, she stayed humble.
quests.explanation: 'Cocky' suggests showy self-confidence, while 'big-headed' is informal.

quests.contextSentence: When the guest speaker described her job, the students seemed curious and kept asking questions.
quests.explanation: 'Uninterested' is neutral, while 'indifferent' suggests not caring either way.

quests.contextSentence: It was considerate of him to turn the music down at night.
quests.explanation: 'Inconsiderate' means not thinking about how your actions affect others, and it's less harsh than 'selfish'.

quests.contextSentence: Since the files contain salaries, choose someone discreet to handle them.
quests.explanation: 'Indiscreet' is the formal negative, and 'loose-lipped' is informal.

quests.contextSentence: The hotel staff were very accommodating about our late arrival.
quests.explanation: 'Rigid' is stronger, suggesting a refusal to bend rules at all.

quests.contextSentence: When the news is sudden and unexpected, people tend to overreact before thinking it through.
quests.explanation: 'Take it in stride' is the idiom for handling bad news without fuss.

quests.contextSentence: Whatever your boss said in the meeting, try to shrug off the criticism; it isn't personal.
quests.explanation: 'Take it to heart' means being deeply affected by a comment.
quests.instruction: Choose the exact opposite of "shrug off".

quests.contextSentence: Despite the stress it causes, most staff secretly look forward to the annual review.
quests.explanation: 'Look forward to' takes -ing: I look forward to seeing you.
quests.instruction: Choose the exact opposite of "look forward to".

quests.contextSentence: Before I tell you the company's plans, can you keep a secret? It isn't public yet.
quests.explanation: 'Let it slip' means revealing a secret by accident, while 'spill the beans' can be deliberate.
quests.instruction: Choose the exact opposite of "keep a secret".

quests.contextSentence: Whenever he's nervous in meetings with senior staff, he tends to ramble for ages.
quests.explanation: 'Cut to the chase' is the common idiom for the same thing.

quests.contextSentence: Instead of announcing it, she only hinted that she might resign.
quests.explanation: 'Spell it out' is the idiom for explaining something in very clear detail.

quests.contextSentence: Judging by the early reviews, the new phone will exceed our expectations.
quests.explanation: Exceed and fall short of both take an object: exceed a target, fall short of a target.

quests.contextSentence: After a few lessons, many beginners overestimate their driving skill.
quests.explanation: The over-/under- pattern repeats in overpaid/underpaid and overrated/underrated.

quests.contextSentence: Despite the clever trailer, the ending of the film was predictable.
quests.explanation: 'Unexpected' is the neutral synonym.

quests.contextSentence: Against everyone's advice, they decided to marry after only six months.
quests.explanation: 'Marry someone' takes no 'with', while 'get married to' uses 'to'.

quests.contextSentence: However loud the argument, close friends usually make up within a day or two.
quests.explanation: British speakers say fall out with someone; Americans say have a falling-out.
quests.instruction: Choose the exact opposite of "make up".

quests.contextSentence: Although we've worked together for years, I only know her as an acquaintance.
quests.explanation: 'Best friend' tops the scale, while 'contact' describes a professional link.

quests.contextSentence: If we want a fair culture, schools should reward honest behaviour openly.
quests.explanation: 'Penalise' fits sport and business, while 'discipline' fits school and work rules.

quests.contextSentence: Some managers blame the team when a project is late.
quests.explanation: 'Credit someone with' means recognising their contribution: she was credited with the idea.

quests.contextSentence: When the patient began to shake with fear, the nurse gently tried to soothe the anxious man.
quests.explanation: 'Provoke' means deliberately causing an angry reaction.
